items.title: Michael White interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 10, 2025
items.q: my family, they all knew the musicians in my family, they had all played with Papa John and Willie Joseph and Earl Pouchet, who was in the family.

ctx.x: Yeah I mean you know music for a lot of people was not a lucrative profession so I mean that’s part of the reason why you had such a big migration of musicians out of New Orleans in the teens and the twenties. But I think that most of the musicians had other professions. So the thing I think you’re referring to is that it was always said that Buddy Bolden was a barber. And thank God Don Marquis’ book proved that wrong. You know bits in jazz are like grass, they’re everywhere. But Buddy Bolden became – he was a…

I have a question about jazz and art and entertainment. Jazz is now in all the universities, and Jazz at Lincoln Center, it’s all wonderful. But I was just reading – I wrote a review on this, there’s a new book out and this fellow spoke about Gunther Schuller and how he approached early jazz more as an art form and this particular author does not apologize at all for the – it was entertainment. So I’m trying to form a question, Michael. Do you think that the musicians back then thought of what they were doing as…
